# DSP reference fixture

`dsp-reference.txt` is generated by `tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c` against ciglet commit `895ba9b1c0eabee83d3544208bbc82420efa3206`, with GCC on Ubuntu x86_64 and `-DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99`, linking `-lm`. Values are printed with nine significant digits to preserve binary32 results on round-trip parsing.

This fixture checks vector statistics, six precise window functions, and frame padding. A maximum absolute error of `1e-7` passes the current Windows MSVC x86_64 and i686 comparisons. This is a scoped threshold for these inputs, not a tolerance claim covering all DSP algorithms or all input sizes.

Compile with `gcc -DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99 -I<upstream> tests/reference/dsp_oracle.c -lm -o dsp-oracle`, then capture `dsp-oracle` output. The fixture does not require linking the upstream library because these tested reference functions are inline definitions in `ciglet.h`.

Intentional corrections: empty statistical inputs return errors or `None`; invalid vector sizes return errors; singleton windows are unity instead of dividing by zero; sorting uses deterministic total ordering and preserves the original index order of equal values.

The FFT fixtures c-fft-f32.bin and c-fft-f64.bin use the pinned unmodified ciglet.c and external/fftsg_h.c compiled with FP_TYPE=float and FP_TYPE=double respectively. tests/reference/fft_oracle.c writes 240 records and 92,112 scalar outputs per precision. Cases cover lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 256, 512, and 1024; impulses, deterministic complex signals, and large DC offsets; all four present/absent real/imaginary combinations; and both transform directions. The C build uses -O2 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections -lm, without -Ofast or fast-math. Section removal allows unused ciglet subsystems to remain unlinked. No upstream source is modified.

Binary format: ASCII FFT1, little-endian uint32 scalar byte width and record count, then uint32 length/scenario/component-mask/inverse fields per record followed by interleaved real/imaginary scalars. This fixture is generated on Ubuntu x86_64, whose native byte order is little-endian; Rust decodes it explicitly.

Across Windows MSVC x86_64/i686, Windows GNU x86_64, and Linux GNU x86_64/i686, all eight integration tests pass. Maximum absolute differences across these targets are 2.288818359375e-5 for f32 and 1.1368683772161603e-13 for f64. Errors normalized by max(1, maximum input component magnitude) times length for forward transforms, or by the same input magnitude for normalized inverse transforms, were at most 3.3527612686157227e-8 and 1.1102230246251565e-16 respectively. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, allowing platform/backend variation while remaining close to measured errors. These are scoped kernel thresholds, not complete speech-feature or inference tolerances. Independent round-trip and Parseval checks validate normalization; frequency-shift checks cover odd/even/singleton/empty sequences against the original inline ordering.

The direct inverse DFT fixtures c-idft-f32.bin and c-idft-f64.bin use tests/reference/idft_oracle.c with the same pinned unmodified C source and compiler flags as the FFT oracle. A reproducible POSIX command from the crate root is shown below; set CIGLET_UPSTREAM to the pinned checkout and repeat with FP_TYPE=double for the f64 fixture. The IDF1 format uses the same field layout as FFT1, with 120 records and 3,552 scalar outputs per precision. Lengths 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 16, 31, and 64 include non-power-of-two and prime cases, with the same three input families and four component-presence combinations. Every record uses the normalized inverse convention. Independent tests verify constant-spectrum cancellation, the positive imaginary sign of a known four-point inverse, all-zero absent inputs, and invalid shape/length errors. This implementation retains quadratic complexity and scalar arithmetic order; the FFT API remains available for power-of-two lengths.

```sh
gcc -O2 -DFP_TYPE=float -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -I"$CIGLET_UPSTREAM" tests/reference/idft_oracle.c "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/ciglet.c" "$CIGLET_UPSTREAM/external/fftsg_h.c" -Wl,--gc-sections -lm -o idft-oracle
./idft-oracle tests/fixtures/c-idft-f32.bin
```

Across the five required native targets, the tested f32 inverse DFT values match C exactly. The largest observed f64 absolute difference is 1.1368683772161603e-13, with normalized error 5.551115123125783e-17. Acceptance thresholds are 2e-7 for f32 and 1e-15 for f64, using max(1, maximum input component magnitude) as the inverse-transform scale. These thresholds apply only to the recorded direct inverse DFT cases.
